articles.summary: Projected heating patterns program the stiffness landscape of a shape-memory-polymer surface. Spatial and temporal modulation tune wave transmission and vibration modes. This informs adaptive resonant structures, without demonstrating a physiological sensor; the preprint is not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Fourier Crosstalk and Leakage Correction for Binary-Encoded Fourier Single-Pixel Imaging
articles.summary: A response-matrix model separates sampled-frequency crosstalk from unsampled leakage in binary Fourier imaging. Simulations and experiments compare iterative and closed-form corrections without modifying acquisition patterns. This provides a transferable calibration principle; the preprint is not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Excitable mechanical lattice: from single-unit bifurcations to boundary-driven pulse propagation
articles.summary: A forced excitable mechanical lattice filters and regularizes pulse trains. Bifurcation analysis links drive amplitude and frequency to propagation behavior. This is adjacent theory for physical signal processing rather than a demonstrated biosensor, and is not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Harnessing smartwatches to spot undiagnosed hypertension
articles.summary: This research highlight discusses smartwatch-based opportunistic hypertension screening. It covers an already delivered prospective study rather than a new independent trial. The distinction between screening and confirmatory cuff-based diagnosis remains essential.

articles.title: Octopus-Inspired Implants for Rapid Deployment and Active Localization of Biochemical Abnormalities
articles.summary: A battery-free implant separates a magnetically navigable electrochemical probe from its resonant wireless module. The reported demonstrations include rapid deployment, pH resolution of 0.1 and active biochemical localization in abdominal and intracranial settings. This directly informs spatially adaptive implants, but the preprint is not peer reviewed and clinical reliability remains unestablished.

articles.title: An ingestible bioelectronic capsule for in vivo DNA monitoring in the gastrointestinal tract
articles.summary: A capsule integrates sampling, lysis, CRISPR-based DNA recognition and wireless readout. Canine and porcine gastric demonstrations target Salmonella DNA, while Helicobacter detection includes human volunteer samples. Human samples are distinct from an in-human capsule trial; this preprint is not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Reaction-driven ionic remodeling enables durable soft electronics
articles.summary: Reaction-controlled ionic remodeling stabilizes soft conductor interfaces. The gel reportedly retains over 90% conductivity after two years in ambient storage, while integrated sensor/transistor tests span seven days. Storage retention must not be conflated with two-year device operation; this preprint is not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Programmable Ultrasound Fields from a Single Laser Pulse
articles.summary: Spatially patterned laser excitation programs broadband fields in a photoacoustic transducer. Experiments demonstrate planar and multiple-focus fields with model agreement in the acoustic near field. The method may transfer to compact acoustic actuation, without proving deep-tissue performance; it is not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Bio-CM²: Distributed computational optics for cortex-wide cellular imaging
articles.summary: Four optical modules share one sensor to combine a 7.5 × 10 mm² field with cellular imaging. Demonstrations include vascular dynamics and more than 3,000 neurons in head-fixed mice. The distributed architecture informs multiscale readout, but should not be described as free-behavior mouse imaging; this preprint is not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Unsupervised chemical-space organization enables identification of self-healing yet ultra-robust polyurethane elastomers
articles.summary: A literature-informed chemical-space workflow selects polyurethane candidates for experimental comparison. The resulting material reports approximately 98 MPa tensile strength and healing after 24 h at 80 °C with water. The method may inform durable flexible substrates, but does not establish body-temperature self-healing; the preprint is not peer reviewed.

articles.summary: NeuroAxis uses endogenous glucose to power closed-loop neuromodulation without batteries or wireless power transfer. The abstract reports improved glycaemic control and reduced inflammation in rat models of type 1 and type 2 diabetes, with effects persisting after treatment cessation. It directly links autonomous implant power, metabolic feedback and bioelectronic therapy; human efficacy is not established.

articles.title: Glucose-powered implant brings devices for treating diabetes a step closer
articles.readingBasis: Official indexed abstract or publicly accessible preview; full text and SI not read
articles.summary: This News and Views discusses the NeuroAxis glucose-powered implant reported in a separate research article. The accessible preview explains the motivation for automatically monitoring and controlling glucose and notes proof-of-principle efficacy in diabetic rats. articles.title: Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin
articles.readingBasis: Official indexed abstract or publicly accessible preview; full text and SI not read
articles.summary: Compression creates additional transient contacts between filaments in dense, weakly connected branched-actin networks. Contacts trapped during growth under force help explain adaptive stiffness beyond standard elastic-network models. The mechanism may inform nonlinear tissue-mechanics interpretation and fibrous sensor interfaces, without demonstrating a sensor device.

articles.title: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues
articles.readingBasis: Official indexed abstract or publicly accessible preview; full text and SI not read
articles.summary: Engineered small-intestinal and colonic barriers combine multilineage epithelium, mucus, an accessible microbial compartment and tissue-resident immune cells. Official summaries describe single-cell characterization of epithelial responses to Salmonella. These controlled host–microbe interfaces offer an adjacent validation environment for mucosal sensing, rather than evidence of an integrated sensor.

articles.title: AI wearables could exploit people’s most vulnerable moments
articles.readingBasis: Official indexed abstract or publicly accessible preview; full text and SI not read
articles.summary: This correspondence argues that adding AI to consumer wearables and smart glasses can introduce harms beyond conventional privacy concerns. The accessible opening frames the ethical issue without providing an engineering performance study. It is relevant to responsible continuous monitoring; the complete correspondence was inaccessible.

articles.title: ‘Light and sound’ therapy for Alzheimer’s flops in long-anticipated trial
articles.readingBasis: Official indexed abstract or publicly accessible preview; full text and SI not read
articles.summary: Nature reports that a headset using flickering light and rhythmic sound failed to slow memory loss in an Alzheimer’s trial. Only the official news preview was accessible, so trial methods, subgroup analyses and numerical outcomes were not independently assessed here. The report offers a translational caution for neuromodulation devices rather than a newly verified efficacy claim.

articles.title: Sex differences in activity thresholds
articles.readingBasis: Official indexed abstract or publicly accessible preview; full text and SI not read
articles.summary: This Matters Arising questions whether common accelerometer thresholds measure equivalent physical-activity doses in women and men. It argues that threshold assumptions can affect inferred dose–response relationships with coronary heart disease. The discussion directly informs wearable-biomarker calibration and should not be presented as a new intervention trial.

articles.title: Interplay of duration and intensity
articles.readingBasis: Official indexed abstract or publicly accessible preview; full text and SI not read
articles.summary: This response discusses the relation between activity duration, intensity and sex-specific recommendations. The accessible opening situates it as a reply about accelerometer-derived physical activity and coronary heart disease. articles.title: A zero-shot spillover denoiser for highly multiplexed images
articles.readingBasis: Official indexed abstract or publicly accessible preview; full text and SI not read
articles.summary: SpillOT uses input-image-only learning and optimal transport to reduce noise and cross-channel spillover in multiplexed biological images. The abstract reports evaluation on imaging mass cytometry and multiplexed immunofluorescence without additional spillover-calibration experiments. Its separation of true signal from structured contamination may inform multichannel sensor reconstruction, a transfer interpretation rather than an existing magnetic-sensor result.

Eight selected details and expanded ordered authors were read. Day-level dates do not verify 03:30 boundary times; subset pagination was not exhausted.
